slot.brief: Object covers successive parts of a journey with different speeds (e.g., halves of distance at two speeds); compute average speed and see why it is not the arithmetic mean.

stem: A cyclist covers the first half of a journey at $12$ m s$^{-1}$ and the second half at $8$ m s$^{-1}$. What is the average speed for the whole journey?

verdicts.working: For equal distances, average speed = 2v₁v₂/(v₁+v₂) = 2(12)(8)/(12+8) = 9.6 m s⁻¹.

working:
For equal distances $d$, $v_{\text{avg}}=\dfrac{2d}{d/12+d/8}=\dfrac{2(12)(8)}{12+8}=9.6$ m s$^{-1}$.

Independent check: For equal distances, average speed = 2v₁v₂/(v₁+v₂) = 2(12)(8)/(12+8) = 9.6 m s⁻¹.
solution:
For equal distances, average speed is the harmonic mean of the two speeds:
$$v_{\text{avg}}=\frac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2}=\frac{2(12)(8)}{12+8}=9.6\text{ m s}^{-1}.$$
